summary.tldr: Sets Criminal Code trial-time limits for superior and provincial court cases, with exceptions for defence-caused delay and some offences.
what_it_does: Creates a rule that a superior court judge must stay proceedings, or stop the case, if the time from charge to the end of trial goes over 30 months, unless the prosecutor proves exceptional circumstances.
Creates a rule that a provincial court judge must stay proceedings if the time from charge to the end of trial goes over 18 months, unless the prosecutor proves exceptional circumstances.
Excludes delay caused only by the defence, or delay the defence waives, when counting whether either time limit has been reached.
Exempts primary designated offences under section 487.04 from these time limits, and says that exemption applies despite paragraph 11(b) of the Charter.
summary.background: The bill says it codifies the Supreme Court of Canada framework from R. v. Jordan on the right to be tried within a reasonable time, and adds exceptions.
